name: Associate Degree Nursing (A45110)
sourceWorkbook: Southeastern CC: what the nursing dean and director told the owner on 2026-10-28 (sequence, eight-week sessions, rotations, group sizes, the NUR 111 lab split, the preceptorship, class size, workload); the ADN and LPN-to-ADN admission pages, the Nursing program page, the campus facilities list, the 2026–27 academic calendar, the NC Board of Nursing 2024 approved-programs list (140 students at one time) and 2021–2023 pass rates; course hours and credits from the NCCCS A45110 standard — compiled 2026-10-28
maxCohortNote: Class size 60 — the program's own figure (2026-10-28): physical resources (the testing lab, classroom seating) support about 60 traditional admissions, 60 to 70 is what it aspires to admit, and NUR 111 has 42 students in Fall 2026. The NC Board of Nursing's 140 is the ADN program's total enrollment at any one time across both years, not an admission number, so each fall's intake depends on second-year retention.
weeklyHoursNote: Term hours per student are the catalog's weekly contact hours × 16 (the 16-week basis), whatever the term's length: the sessions carry them, the posted days, times and rooms place them. Hours and credits are the NCCCS course standard's. The program runs every NUR course but 111 and 213 as an eight-week session (A-Term / B-Term in fall and spring; the eight-week summer session from Jun 1 inside the college's 10-week term, May 17 – Jul 27, 2027), so those courses' sessions sit in eight of the term's weeks at twice the catalog's weekly hours. Days and times beyond NUR 111's Tuesday lab, Thursday lab sections and Wednesday clinical come with the Fall 2026 schedule (due Dec 4).

courses.title: Introduction to Health Concepts
courses.requisites: Admission to the program; NUR 117 Pharmacology within five years
courses.description: Introduces the concepts within the three domains of the individual, healthcare and nursing: medication administration, assessment, nutrition, ethics, interdisciplinary teams, informatics, evidence-based practice, individual-centered care and quality improvement. Sixteen weeks (the program runs its other NUR courses as eight-week sessions). Clinical on hospital medical-surgical units on Wednesdays, with the early weeks on campus in the skills and simulation labs; one group a week rotates into the simulation lab when the coordinator is free to staff it. The six-hour lab is split: Tuesday the whole cohort in the classroom for the lab's instruction, Thursday two sections of thirty in the lab. Hours and credits are the NCCCS standard's; the term placement is the program's own (stated 2026-10-28) — the course-sequence document due Dec 4 confirms it.
